sanskrit: amaraṃ yājyam āsādya mām ṛṣe mā sma mānuṣam yājayethā maruttaṃ tvaṃ martyadharmāṇam āturam
english: Having found in me an immortal as your sacrificer, O seer, do not perform the rites for a mortal — for Marutta, who is bound by the law of mortals and afflicted.

sanskrit: spardhate ca mayā vipra sadā vai sa hi pārthivaḥ evam astv iti cāpy ukto bhrātrā te balavṛtrahā
english: That king is forever contending with me, O brahmin. And when your brother, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra, was thus addressed, he answered, "So be it."

sanskrit: sa mām abhigataṃ premṇā yājyavan na bubhūṣati devarājam upāśritya tad viddhi munipuṃgava
english: Though I came to him with affection, he does not wish to treat me as his sacrificer, having taken refuge with the king of the gods — know this, O bull among sages.

sanskrit: so 'ham icchāmi bhavatā sarvasvenāpi yājitum kāmaye samatikrāntuṃ vāsavaṃ tvatkṛtair guṇaiḥ
english: Therefore I wish to have you officiate at my sacrifice, even at the cost of all I possess. I long to surpass Vāsava through the merits you would bring about.

sanskrit: na hi me vartate buddhir gantuṃ brahman bṛhaspatim pratyākhyāto hi tenāsmi tathānapakṛte sati
english: For my mind is not inclined, O brahmin, to go to Bṛhaspati: I was rejected by him, though I had done him no wrong.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca cikīrṣasi yathākāmaṃ sarvam etat tvayi dhruvam yadi sarvān abhiprāyān kartāsi mama pārthiva
english: Saṃvarta said: All this you desire to accomplish at will rests firmly upon you — if, O king, you carry out every one of my intentions.

sanskrit: yājyamānaṃ mayā hi tvāṃ bṛhaspatipuraṃdarau dviṣetāṃ samabhikruddhāv etad ekaṃ samarthaya
english: For when I officiate at your sacrifice, both Bṛhaspati and Purandara will hate you, inflamed with wrath. To this one thing you must steel yourself.

sanskrit: sthairyam atra kathaṃ te syāt sa tvaṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ kuru kupitas tvāṃ na hīdānīṃ bhasma kuryāṃ sabāndhavam
english: How will you remain steadfast in this? Make yourself free of doubt — lest, enraged, I now reduce you to ashes together with your kinsmen.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca yāvat tapet sahasrāṃśus tiṣṭheraṃś cāpi parvatāḥ tāval lokān na labheyaṃ tyajeyaṃ saṃgataṃ yadi
english: Marutta said: As long as the thousand-rayed sun shall burn, and as long as the mountains shall stand — for that long may I gain no worlds, if ever I abandon our compact.

sanskrit: mā cāpi śubhabuddhitvaṃ labheyam iha karhi cit samyag jñāne vaiṣaye vā tyajeyaṃ saṃgataṃ yadi
english: And may I never attain a wholesome understanding here, whether in true knowledge or in worldly matters, if ever I abandon our compact.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca āvikṣita śubhā buddhir dhīyatāṃ tava karmasu yājanaṃ hi mamāpy evaṃ vartate tvayi pārthiva
english: Saṃvarta said: O son of Avikṣit, let an auspicious resolve settle upon your undertakings, for my own intent to officiate for you, O king, stands likewise firm.

sanskrit: saṃvidhāsye ca te rājann akṣayaṃ dravyam uttamam yena devān sagandharvāñ śakraṃ cābhibhaviṣyasi
english: And I shall provide for you, O king, an inexhaustible store of the finest wealth, by which you shall overcome the gods together with the gandharvas, and Śakra as well.

sanskrit: na tu me vartate buddhir dhane yājyeṣu vā punaḥ vipriyaṃ tu cikīrṣāmi bhrātuś cendrasya cobhayoḥ
english: My mind, however, is not set upon wealth, nor again upon those for whom I officiate; rather, I wish to do what displeases both my brother and Indra.

sanskrit: gamayiṣyāmi cendreṇa samatām api te dhruvam priyaṃ ca te kariṣyāmi satyam etad bravīmi te
english: And I shall surely bring you to equality even with Indra, and I shall do what pleases you — this I tell you in truth.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca girer himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe muñjavān nāma parvataḥ tapyate yatra bhagavāṃs tapo nityam umāpatiḥ
english: Saṃvarta said: On the back of Mount Himavat there is a mountain named Muñjavān, where the blessed lord, the consort of Umā, ever practises his austerities.

sanskrit: vanaspatīnāṃ mūleṣu ṭaṅkeṣu śikhareṣu ca guhāsu śailarājasya yathākāmaṃ yathāsukham
english: Among the roots of the great trees, in the chasms and on the peaks, in the caverns of that king of mountains, he dwells as he wills and at his ease.

sanskrit: umāsahāyo bhagavān yatra nityaṃ maheśvaraḥ āste śūlī mahātejā nānābhūtagaṇāvṛtaḥ
english: There the blessed Maheśvara, bearer of the trident, of mighty splendour, abides forever with Umā for his companion, surrounded by hosts of varied beings.

sanskrit: tatra rudrāś ca sādhyāś ca viśve 'tha vasavas tathā yamaś ca varuṇaś caiva kuberaś ca sahānugaḥ
english: There are the Rudras and the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas and the Vasus too, and Yama and Varuṇa, and Kubera with his retinue.

sanskrit: bhūtāni ca piśācāś ca nāsatyāv aśvināv api gandharvāpsarasaś caiva yakṣā devarṣayas tathā
english: And there are the spirits and the piśācas, the Nāsatyas, the two Aśvins, the gandharvas and apsarases, the yakṣas, and the divine seers as well.

sanskrit: ādityā marutaś caiva yātudhānāś ca sarvaśaḥ upāsante mahātmānaṃ bahurūpam umāpatim
english: The Ādityas and the Maruts, and the yātudhānas in their every kind, all wait upon the great-souled, many-formed consort of Umā.

sanskrit: ramate bhagavāṃs tatra kuberānucaraiḥ saha vikṛtair vikṛtākāraiḥ krīḍadbhiḥ pṛthivīpate śriyā jvalan dṛśyate vai bālādityasamadyutiḥ
english: There the blessed lord takes his delight among the followers of Kubera — deformed beings of misshapen aspect, sporting about him, O lord of earth — and blazing with glory he is seen, radiant as the rising sun.

sanskrit: na rūpaṃ dṛśyate tasya saṃsthānaṃ vā kathaṃ cana nirdeṣṭuṃ prāṇibhiḥ kaiś cit prākṛtair māṃsalocanaiḥ
english: His form cannot be seen, nor in any way his shape made out or described by any ordinary creatures whose eyes are but of flesh.

sanskrit: noṣṇaṃ na śiśiraṃ tatra na vāyur na ca bhāskaraḥ na jarā kṣutpipāse vā na mṛtyur na bhayaṃ nṛpa
english: There is no heat there nor cold, no wind nor sun, no old age, neither hunger nor thirst, no death and no fear, O king.

sanskrit: tasya śailasya pārśveṣu sarveṣu jayatāṃ vara dhātavo jātarūpasya raśmayaḥ savitur yathā
english: On all the slopes of that mountain, O best of conquerors, are veins of gold, gleaming like the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: rakṣyante te kuberasya sahāyair udyatāyudhaiḥ cikīrṣadbhiḥ priyaṃ rājan kuberasya mahātmanaḥ
english: These are guarded by Kubera's companions with weapons upraised, who wish, O king, to do what pleases the great-souled Kubera.

sanskrit: tasmai bhagavate kṛtvā namaḥ śarvāya vedhase rudrāya śitikaṇṭhāya surūpāya suvarcase
english: Having made obeisance to that blessed one — to Śarva the ordainer, to Rudra, to the blue-throated, to the fair-formed, to the radiant —

sanskrit: kapardine karālāya haryakṣṇe varadāya ca tryakṣṇe pūṣṇo dantabhide vāmanāya śivāya ca
english: to the wearer of matted locks, to the terrible, to the tawny-eyed and the granter of boons, to the three-eyed, to the breaker of Pūṣan's teeth, to the dwarfish and to Śiva,

sanskrit: yāmyāyāvyaktakeśāya sadvṛtte śaṃkarāya ca kṣemyāya harinetrāya sthāṇave puruṣāya ca
english: to the deathly one, to him whose hair is unrevealed, to the well-conducted and to Śaṃkara, to the giver of peace, to the green-eyed, to the unmoving pillar and to the Person,

sanskrit: harikeśāya muṇḍāya kṛśāyottāraṇāya ca bhāskarāya sutīrthāya devadevāya raṃhase
english: to the tawny-haired, to the shaven-headed, to the lean one and to the deliverer, to the sun-like, to the holy ford, to the god of gods, to the swift one,

sanskrit: uṣṇīṣiṇe suvaktrāya sahasrākṣāya mīḍhuṣe giriśāya praśāntāya yataye cīravāsase
english: to the turbaned, to the fair-faced, to the thousand-eyed, to the bountiful, to the mountain-dweller, to the tranquil, to the ascetic clad in rags,

sanskrit: bilvadaṇḍāya siddhāya sarvadaṇḍadharāya ca mṛgavyādhāya mahate dhanvine 'tha bhavāya ca
english: to him whose staff is of bilva-wood, to the perfected, to the bearer of every rod of chastisement, to the great hunter of beasts, to the wielder of the bow, and to Bhava,

sanskrit: varāya saumyavaktrāya paśuhastāya varṣiṇe hiraṇyabāhave rājann ugrāya pataye diśām
english: to the excellent, to the gentle-faced, to him whose hand holds the sacrificial beast, to the rainer of blessings, to the golden-armed, O king, to the fierce, to the lord of the quarters,

sanskrit: paśūnāṃ pataye caiva bhūtānāṃ pataye tathā vṛṣāya mātṛbhaktāya senānye madhyamāya ca
english: and to the lord of creatures, to the lord of beings likewise, to the bull, to the devotee of the Mothers, to the leader of armies and to the one in the midst,

sanskrit: sruvahastāya pataye dhanvine bhārgavāya ca ajāya kṛṣṇanetrāya virūpākṣāya caiva ha
english: to him whose hand holds the sacrificial ladle, to the lord, to the bowman and to Bhārgava, to the unborn, to the dark-eyed, and to the one of unsymmetrical eyes,

sanskrit: tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrāya tīkṣṇāya vaiśvānaramukhāya ca mahādyutaye 'naṅgāya sarvāṅgāya prajāvate
english: to the sharp-fanged, to the keen, to him whose mouth is the universal fire, to the greatly resplendent, to the bodiless, to the all-bodied, to the lord of progeny,

sanskrit: tathā śukrādhipataye pṛthave kṛttivāsase kapālamāline nityaṃ suvarṇamukuṭāya ca
english: and to the lord of the seed of life, to the broad one, to him clad in a hide, to the wearer of the garland of skulls, and ever to the gold-crowned one,

sanskrit: mahādevāya kṛṣṇāya tryambakāyānaghāya ca krodhanāya nṛśaṃsāya mṛdave bāhuśāline
english: to Mahādeva, to the dark one, to the three-eyed and to the sinless, to the wrathful, to the cruel, to the gentle, to the strong-armed,

sanskrit: daṇḍine taptatapase tathaiva krūrakarmaṇe sahasraśirase caiva sahasracaraṇāya ca namaḥ svadhāsvarūpāya bahurūpāya daṃṣṭriṇe
english: to the rod-bearer, to the practiser of fierce austerity and likewise to him of cruel deeds, to the thousand-headed and to the thousand-footed — obeisance to him whose form is the svadhā offering, to the many-formed, to the fanged one.

sanskrit: pinākinaṃ mahādevaṃ mahāyoginam avyayam triśūlapāṇiṃ varadaṃ tryambakaṃ bhuvaneśvaram
english: To the bearer of the Pināka bow, to Mahādeva, to the great yogin, to the imperishable, to him whose hand holds the trident, to the granter of boons, to the three-eyed, to the lord of the world,

sanskrit: tripuraghnaṃ trinayanaṃ trilokeśaṃ mahaujasam prabhavaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dhāraṇaṃ dharaṇīdharam
english: to the destroyer of the three cities, to the three-eyed, to the lord of the three worlds, to the mighty in vigour, to the source of all beings, to the sustainer, to the upholder of the earth,

sanskrit: īśānaṃ śaṃkaraṃ sarvaṃ śivaṃ viśveśvaraṃ bhavam umāpatiṃ paśupatiṃ viśvarūpaṃ maheśvaram
english: to Īśāna, to Śaṃkara, to the All, to Śiva, to the lord of the universe, to Bhava, to the consort of Umā, to the lord of creatures, to the all-formed, to Maheśvara,

sanskrit: virūpākṣaṃ daśabhujaṃ tiṣyagovṛṣabhadhvajam ugraṃ sthāṇuṃ śivaṃ ghoraṃ śarvaṃ gaurīśam īśvaram
english: to the one of unsymmetrical eyes, to the ten-armed, to him whose banner bears the bull, to the fierce, to the unmoving, to Śiva, to the terrible, to Śarva, to the lord of Gaurī, to the Lord,

sanskrit: śitikaṇṭham ajaṃ śukraṃ pṛthuṃ pṛthuharaṃ haram viśvarūpaṃ virūpākṣaṃ bahurūpam umāpatim
english: to the blue-throated, to the unborn, to the bright, to the broad, to the mighty remover, to Hara, to the all-formed, to the one of unsymmetrical eyes, to the many-formed consort of Umā —

sanskrit: praṇamya śirasā devam anaṅgāṅgaharaṃ haram śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ yāhi mahādevaṃ caturmukham
english: having bowed your head to the god, to Hara who burned away the body of the Bodiless One, go for refuge to the refuge-giving Mahādeva, the four-faced.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtvā namas tasmai mahādevāya raṃhase mahātmane kṣitipate tat suvarṇam avāpsyasi suvarṇam āhariṣyantas tatra gacchantu te narāḥ
english: Having thus made obeisance to that swift and great-souled Mahādeva, O lord of the earth, you shall obtain that gold. Let your men go there to fetch the gold.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca ity uktaḥ sa vacas tasya cakre kāraṃdhamātmajaḥ tato 'timānuṣaṃ sarvaṃ cakre yajñasya saṃvidhim sauvarṇāni ca bhāṇḍāni saṃcakrus tatra śilpinaḥ
english: Vyāsa said: Thus addressed, the son of Kāraṃdhama did as he was bidden. Then he made every preparation for the sacrifice on a superhuman scale, and the craftsmen there fashioned vessels of gold.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatis tu tāṃ śrutvā maruttasya mahīpateḥ samṛddhim ati devebhyaḥ saṃtāpam akarod bhṛśam
english: But Bṛhaspati, hearing of the prosperity of King Marutta, which surpassed even that of the gods, was sorely tormented.

sanskrit: sa tapyamāno vaivarṇyaṃ kṛśatvaṃ cāgamat param bhaviṣyati hi me śatruḥ saṃvarto vasumān iti
english: Tormented thus, he grew utterly pale and wasted, thinking, "Saṃvarta, grown rich, will become my rival."

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā bhṛśasaṃtaptaṃ devarājo bṛhaspatim abhigamyāmaravṛtaḥ provācedaṃ vacas tadā
english: Hearing that Bṛhaspati was grievously distressed, the king of the gods, surrounded by the immortals, went to him and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: indra uvāca kaccit sukhaṃ svapiṣi tvaṃ bṛhaspate; kaccin manojñāḥ paricārakās te kaccid devānāṃ sukhakāmo 'si vipra; kaccid devās tvāṃ paripālayanti
english: Indra said: Do you sleep in comfort, O Bṛhaspati? Are your attendants agreeable to you? Do you wish well to the gods, O brahmin? And do the gods watch over you?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca sukhaṃ śaye 'haṃ śayane mahendra; tathā manojñāḥ paricārakā me tathā devānāṃ sukhakāmo 'smi śakra; devāś ca māṃ subhṛśaṃ pālayanti
english: Bṛhaspati said: I lie in comfort upon my couch, O great Indra; my attendants are indeed agreeable to me; I wish well to the gods, O Śakra; and the gods guard me right closely.

sanskrit: indra uvāca kuto duḥkhaṃ mānasaṃ dehajaṃ vā; pāṇḍur vivarṇaś ca kutas tvam adya ācakṣva me tad dvija yāvad etān; nihanmi sarvāṃs tava duḥkhakartṝn
english: Indra said: Whence then this grief of mind or of body? Why are you today so pale and wan? Tell me of it, O brahmin, that I may slay all those who cause you this sorrow.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca maruttam āhur maghavan yakṣyamāṇaṃ; mahāyajñenottamadakṣiṇena taṃ saṃvarto yājayiteti me śrutaṃ; tad icchāmi na sa taṃ yājayeta
english: Bṛhaspati said: They say, O Maghavan, that Marutta is about to sacrifice with a great rite of bountiful fees; and I have heard that Saṃvarta is to officiate for him. This I wish: that he should not officiate for him.

sanskrit: indra uvāca sarvān kāmān anujāto 'si vipra; yas tvaṃ devānāṃ mantrayase purodhāḥ ubhau ca te janmamṛtyū vyatītau; kiṃ saṃvartas tava kartādya vipra
english: Indra said: You have been granted all your desires, O brahmin, you who counsel the gods as their chaplain; and both birth and death have been transcended by you. What, then, can Saṃvarta do to you today, O brahmin?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca devaiḥ saha tvam asurān saṃpraṇudya; jighāṃsase 'dyāpy uta sānubandhān yaṃ yaṃ samṛddhaṃ paśyasi tatra tatra; duḥkhaṃ sapatneṣu samṛddhabhāvaḥ
english: Bṛhaspati said: Even now, having driven back the asuras with the gods, you still seek to slay them along with their kindred. Wherever you behold one grown prosperous, there is the sorrow of it — that a rival should flourish.

sanskrit: ato 'smi devendra vivarṇarūpaḥ; sapatno me vardhate tan niśamya sarvopāyair maghavan saṃniyaccha; saṃvartaṃ vā pārthivaṃ vā maruttam
english: For this reason, O lord of the gods, my color has faded: my rival grows in power. Hearing this, O Maghavan, restrain by every means either Saṃvarta or King Marutta.

sanskrit: indra uvāca ehi gaccha prahito jātavedo; bṛhaspatiṃ paridātuṃ marutte ayaṃ vai tvā yājayitā bṛhaspatis; tathāmaraṃ caiva kariṣyatīti
english: Indra said: Come, go forth as my envoy, O Jātavedas, to deliver Bṛhaspati over to Marutta, saying: "This Bṛhaspati shall officiate at your sacrifice, and shall likewise make you immortal."

sanskrit: agnir uvāca ayaṃ gacchāmi tava śakrādya dūto; bṛhaspatiṃ paridātuṃ marutte vācaṃ satyāṃ puruhūtasya kartuṃ; bṛhaspateś cāpacitiṃ cikīrṣuḥ
english: Agni said: Here I go today as your envoy, O Śakra, to deliver Bṛhaspati over to Marutta — to make the word of the much-invoked one come true, and wishing to do honor to Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tataḥ prāyād dhūmaketur mahātmā; vanaspatīn vīrudhaś cāvamṛdnan kāmād dhimānte parivartamānaḥ; kāṣṭhātigo mātariśveva nardan
english: Vyāsa said: Then the great-souled, smoke-bannered one set forth, crushing the great trees and the creepers, moving at will about the edge of the snow, swifter than the wind that outstrips the very wood, and roaring.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca āścaryam adya paśyāmi rūpiṇaṃ vahnim āgatam āsanaṃ salilaṃ pādyaṃ gāṃ copānaya vai mune
english: Marutta said: A marvel I behold today — Fire come hither in bodily form! Bring forth a seat, water, an offering for the feet, and a cow, O sage.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca āsanaṃ salilaṃ pādyaṃ pratinandāmi te 'nagha indreṇa tu samādiṣṭaṃ viddhi māṃ dūtam āgatam
english: Agni said: I welcome your seat, your water, your offering for the feet, O sinless one; but know that I have come as an envoy, dispatched by Indra.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca kaccic chrīmān devarājaḥ sukhī ca; kaccic cāsmān prīyate dhūmaketo kaccid devāś cāsya vaśe yathāvat; tad brūhi tvaṃ mama kārtsnyena deva
english: Marutta said: Is the glorious king of the gods well and content? Is he pleased with us, O smoke-bannered one? Are the gods duly under his sway? Tell me all of it in full, O god.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca śakro bhṛśaṃ susukhī pārthivendra; prītiṃ cecchaty ajarāṃ vai tvayā saḥ devāś ca sarve vaśagās tasya rājan; saṃdeśaṃ tvaṃ śṛṇu me devarājñaḥ
english: Agni said: Śakra is most exceedingly content, O lord of kings, and he desires an undying friendship with you. All the gods, O king, are obedient to him. Now hear from me the message of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ māṃ prāhiṇot tvatsakāśaṃ; bṛhaspatiṃ paridātuṃ marutte ayaṃ gurur yājayitā nṛpa tvāṃ; martyaṃ santam amaraṃ tvāṃ karotu
english: For this purpose he sent me into your presence — to deliver Bṛhaspati over to Marutta: let this preceptor officiate at your sacrifice, O king, and though you are mortal, let him make you immortal.

sanskrit: marutta uvāca saṃvarto 'yaṃ yājayitā dvijo me; bṛhaspater añjalir eṣa tasya nāsau devaṃ yājayitvā mahendraṃ; martyaṃ santaṃ yājayann adya śobhet
english: Marutta said: This brahmin Saṃvarta is the one who shall officiate for me; and to Bṛhaspati here are my joined palms in salutation. Having served as priest to the god, the great Indra, it would ill become him today to officiate for one who is mortal.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca ye vai lokā devaloke mahāntaḥ; saṃprāpsyase tān devarājaprasādāt tvāṃ ced asau yājayed vai bṛhaspatir; nūnaṃ svargaṃ tvaṃ jayeḥ kīrtiyuktaḥ
english: Agni said: Those great worlds that are in the realm of the gods, you shall attain through the favor of the king of the gods, if Bṛhaspati should officiate for you; surely you would win heaven, crowned with renown.

sanskrit: tathā lokā mānuṣā ye ca divyāḥ; prajāpateś cāpi ye vai mahāntaḥ te te jitā devarājyaṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ; bṛhaspatiś ced yājayet tvāṃ narendra
english: Likewise the worlds of men and those that are divine, and the great worlds of Prajāpati too — all these would be won by you, and the whole sovereignty of the gods, if Bṛhaspati should officiate for you, O lord of men.

sanskrit: saṃvarta uvāca māsmān evaṃ tvaṃ punar āgāḥ kathaṃ cid; bṛhaspatiṃ paridātuṃ marutte mā tvāṃ dhakṣye cakṣuṣā dāruṇena; saṃkruddho 'haṃ pāvaka tan nibodha
english: Saṃvarta said: Do not come to us again like this, in any wise, to deliver Bṛhaspati over to Marutta — lest I burn you with my dreadful eye when I am enraged, O Pāvaka. Mark this well.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tato devān agamad dhūmaketur; dāhād bhīto vyathito 'śvatthaparṇavat taṃ vai dṛṣṭvā prāha śakro mahātmā; bṛhaspateḥ saṃnidhau havyavāham
english: Vyāsa said: Then the smoke-bannered one went off to the gods, afraid of being burned, trembling like a leaf of the aśvattha tree. Beholding him, the great-souled Śakra spoke to the bearer of oblations in the presence of Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: yat tvaṃ gataḥ prahito jātavedo; bṛhaspatiṃ paridātuṃ marutte tat kiṃ prāha sa nṛpo yakṣyamāṇaḥ; kaccid vacaḥ pratigṛhṇāti tac ca
english: You who were sent and went forth, O Jātavedas, to deliver Bṛhaspati over to Marutta — what did that king, about to sacrifice, say to you? Does he accept the message, or not?

sanskrit: agnir uvāca na te vācaṃ rocayate marutto; bṛhaspater añjaliṃ prāhiṇot saḥ saṃvarto māṃ yājayitety abhīkṣṇaṃ; punaḥ punaḥ sa mayā procyamānaḥ
english: Agni said: Marutta does not relish your word; he offered joined palms in salutation to Bṛhaspati, saying again and again, "Saṃvarta is to officiate for me" — though I urged him repeatedly.

sanskrit: uvācedaṃ mānuṣā ye ca divyāḥ; prajāpater ye ca lokā mahāntaḥ tāṃś cel labheyaṃ saṃvidaṃ tena kṛtvā; tathāpi neccheyam iti pratītaḥ
english: He said this with conviction: "Though I might gain the worlds of men and those that are divine, and the great worlds of Prajāpati, by making a compact with him — even then I would not wish it."

sanskrit: indra uvāca punar bhavān pārthivaṃ taṃ sametya; vākyaṃ madīyaṃ prāpaya svārthayuktam punar yady ukto na kariṣyate vacas; tato vajraṃ saṃprahartāsmi tasmai
english: Indra said: Go once more to that king and convey my word, charged with what is to his own good. If, told again, he will not do my bidding, then I shall hurl the thunderbolt against him.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca gandharvarāḍ yātv ayaṃ tatra dūto; bibhemy ahaṃ vāsava tatra gantum saṃrabdho mām abravīt tīkṣṇaroṣaḥ; saṃvarto vākyaṃ caritabrahmacaryaḥ
english: Agni said: Let this king of the gandharvas go there as the envoy; I am afraid to go there, O Vāsava. Saṃvarta, of fierce wrath, his vow of chastity fulfilled, spoke to me in fury these words:

sanskrit: yady āgaccheḥ punar evaṃ kathaṃ cid; bṛhaspatiṃ paridātuṃ marutte daheyaṃ tvāṃ cakṣuṣā dāruṇena; saṃkruddha ity etad avaihi śakra
english: "If you should come again in any wise like this, to deliver Bṛhaspati over to Marutta, I would burn you with my dreadful eye in my rage." Understand this, O Śakra.

sanskrit: indra uvāca tvam evānyān dahase jātavedo; na hi tvad anyo vidyate bhasmakartā tvatsaṃsparśāt sarvaloko bibhety; aśraddheyaṃ vadase havyavāha
english: Indra said: You yourself are the one who burns others, O Jātavedas, for none other than you is found to reduce things to ashes; the whole world fears your touch. What you say is past belief, O bearer of oblations.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca divaṃ devendra pṛthivīṃ caiva sarvāṃ; saṃveṣṭayes tvaṃ svabalenaiva śakra evaṃvidhasyeha satas tavāsau; kathaṃ vṛtras tridivaṃ prāg jahāra
english: Agni said: Heaven, O king of the gods, and all the earth you could enfold by your own might alone, O Śakra. Yet, you being of such a kind, how was it that Vṛtra once carried off the triple heaven?

sanskrit: indra uvāca na caṇḍikā jaṅgamā no kareṇur; na vārisomaṃ prapibāmi vahne na durbale vai visṛjāmi vajraṃ; ko me 'sukhāya praharen manuṣyaḥ
english: Indra said: I am no slayer of the small and helpless, no creeping thing nor she-elephant; I do not drink mere water in place of soma, O Fire, nor do I loose the thunderbolt upon the weak. What mortal could strike at me to my hurt?

sanskrit: pravrājayeyaṃ kālakeyān pṛthivyām; apākarṣaṃ dānavān antarikṣāt divaḥ prahrādam avasānam ānayaṃ; ko me 'sukhāya prahareta martyaḥ
english: I drove the Kālakeyas into exile upon the earth; I dragged the dānavas down from the firmament; I brought Prahrāda from heaven to his final end. What mortal could strike at me to my hurt?

sanskrit: agnir uvāca yatra śaryātiṃ cyavano yājayiṣyan; sahāśvibhyāṃ somam agṛhṇad ekaḥ taṃ tvaṃ kruddhaḥ pratyaṣedhīḥ purastāc; charyātiyajñaṃ smara taṃ mahendra
english: Agni said: When Cyavana, about to officiate for Śaryāti, took the soma single-handed together with the Aśvins, you in your anger sought to forbid it of old — recall that sacrifice of Śaryāti, O great Indra.
